notes:
VERIFIED-CLEAN START: the stopped 6-minute-backoff attempt left no trace on TP-1632/48319 (name and updated_at unchanged, matched the clone-time baseline exactly) and TP-1616/48283 was still in the exact byte-identical state clone_test_plan_v1 last verified (updated_at 2026-09-18T12:53:05.000Z, sub_plans_count 14, name/description/tags all matching) — confirmed by reading, not assumed.

WRAPPER QUESTION — SETTLED, and the create_test_plan_v1 500 does NOT generalize: guidance for update_test_plan_v1 makes the same wrap-required claim that made create_test_plan_v1 unusable, but the outcome here is different and better. Flat body -> clean 200, correctly updated, correctly persisted (re-read confirmed). Nested body -> rejected CLIENT-SIDE before any HTTP call, with an explicit, helpful error naming the accepted flat fields and telling the caller to send them directly (not a 500, not an ambiguous failure). So: (1) the guidance's wrapper claim is wrong here too — same DRIFT family as create_test_plan_v1 and update_test_plan_v2 — but (2) unlike create_test_plan_v1, the flat body that actually works does NOT 500; it succeeds cleanly. This RULES OUT the theory that the entity's whole write surface degraded — update_test_plan_v1's flat-body path is healthy, and preprod v1 was demonstrably reachable and correct throughout this probe (ruling out the earlier outage as an explanation for anything found here). The create_test_plan_v1 500 remains an isolated defect on that one capability, not evidence of a broader entity-wide write failure.

PUT-VS-PATCH — SETTLED: this capability behaves as a PARTIAL/PATCH-style update, not a full-object replace, despite `update_test_plan_v1` sounding like it could overwrite the whole record. Sending a body containing ONLY `name` left every other field exactly as it was: tags stayed [], owner (2522) and assignee unchanged, start_date/end_date stayed null, custom_fields/attachments/issues stayed empty, sub_plans_count stayed 0, and test_runs_count stayed {active:1,closed:0} — only `name` and `updated_at` changed. One minor exception worth flagging: `description` flipped from an empty string ("") pre-update to a bare `null` post-update, even though `description` was never included in the request body — a small representation drift (empty-string vs null), not real data loss, but it means 'omitted field' is not perfectly idempotent for every field the way it is for owner/tags/dates in this same response.

RUN LINK — CONFIRMED STILL LINKED: get_test_plan_test_runs_v1(48319) before AND after the rename both show exactly one run, TR-9111 (uuid 17578623), still attached. The update, which never sent a `test_runs` key at all, did not unlink it — consistent with the guidance's claim that omitting `test_runs` 'leaves the linkage alone.' No unintended unlink occurred; the existence of a dedicated `unlink_test_runs_from_test_plan` capability is corroborated as the only deliberate path to break this link, not a side effect of a rename.

UPDATED_AT DOES MOVE: pre-update, TP-1632's updated_at (2026-09-21T13:44:07.000Z) was byte-identical to created_at, i.e. genuinely untouched since the clone. Post-update it became 2026-09-22T05:11:26.000Z — a real, live-verified bump on a genuine content edit. This is the opposite of update_filter's already-documented inert `entity`/`updated_at` under a 200; update_test_plan_v1 does move the clock when something actually changes.

READER DISAGREEMENT — RE-CHECKED POST-UPDATE, STILL SYSTEMIC: get_test_plan_test_runs_v1(48319) independently confirms TR-9111 linked (one row, present, matching uuid). get_test_runs_v1(project_id=379335744, include_test_plan='true') was re-read in the same pass and STILL shows test_plans:[] for TR-9111 (row present on page 1, test_plans empty), reproducing the exact defect already confirmed systemic in clone_test_plan_v1's probe. The write side is proven correct (one reader shows the link); get_test_runs_v1 with include_test_plan=true remains the one broken reader, now confirmed across three separate runs (TR-9061, and now TR-9111 both before and after an unrelated plan edit) and two separate probes on two different days — ruling out staleness/caching as an explanation.

COUNT-VS-ROWS: test_runs_count={active:1,closed:0} on the updated plan matches the single actual row returned by get_test_plan_test_runs_v1 — no desync observed here.

CONTRACT COMPLETENESS: declared `returns` includes `reviewers`, but the actual 200 body has no `reviewers` key anywhere (not null, just absent) — shallowest missing path, since no reviewers were ever configured on this plan and a reviewers-only edit was never attempted (out of scope for 'update only the name'). Three fields returned but never declared in `returns`: `test_plan_progress` (guidance elsewhere calls this always-{} legacy, matches observation of {}), `test_results_trend` (null here), and `test_results_trend_v2` (populated). These three exactly match the same undeclared-field DRIFT already recorded against the sibling read capability get_test_plan_by_integer_id_v1 (tests/live/runs/tm/get_test_plan_by_integer_id_v1.json) — expected, since this capability's success body is described as 'the plan, re-read' using the same underlying shape.
